description: The chart illustrates the number of hateful communication datasets per year, broken down by researcher location categories shown in the legend. The horizontal axis lists the categories as years from 2012 through 2022 in chronological order and is labeled “Year.” The vertical axis is labeled “Number of datasets” and uses a logarithmic scale with major tick marks at approximately \(10^0\), \(10^1\), and \(10^2\) (about 1, 10, and 100), spanning roughly from 1 up to a bit above 100. For each year, multiple narrow, side-by-side colored bars represent locations: Other (blue), USA (orange), IN (green), UK (red), IT (purple), and DE (brown), with no stacking; not every location appears in every year. Early years show sparse bars near 1–3 datasets (e.g., USA around 2 in 2012 and 2013; Other around 2 in 2014 and around 3 in 2015; DE around 1 in 2015). From 2016 onward, grouped bars appear more consistently, with approximate values such as 2016 showing USA around 7, Other around 4, IN around 3, and UK around 2; 2017 showing Other around the high teens, USA around the mid-teens, UK around ~9, IT around ~5, and IN near ~1; 2018 showing Other around ~30, USA around ~12, and IN/UK/IT/DE clustered around ~4; 2019 showing Other around ~50, USA around ~16, IN around ~6, IT around ~8, and UK around ~2; 2020 showing Other around ~90, USA around ~35, IN around ~12, UK around ~15, IT around ~2, and DE around ~18; and 2021 showing the tallest bar for Other slightly above \(10^2\) (just over 100), with USA around ~40, IN around ~20, UK around ~17, IT around ~12, and DE around ~9. In 2022, a lighter, semi-transparent set of bars appears for multiple locations, with approximate heights around ~20 for Other, ~9 for IN, ~8 for UK, ~3 for USA, and ~1 for IT. The bars are not sorted by height within each year, and there are no explicit annotations or special emphasis beyond the color legend and the lighter styling used for the 2022 bars.
